lots.title: Ely Library - Engage, Design and Fit Out
lots.description: Single-lot design-and-build contract for Cambridgeshire County Council to refresh Ely Library's public offer. Scope covers stakeholder engagement (site visit, staff/Friends group consultation), initial design proposals with at least one feedback round incorporated, and the subsequent supply and installation of furniture, signage and carpet within the main library footprint of ~850sqm (first-floor, ~150k visits/year, ~100k issues/year). Out-of-scope items include the main entrance/stairway facade completed in 2022 and provision of power, data, public PCs and self-service machines (delivered by the Authority's IT and electrical contractors, though the design must accommodate them).
requirements: Design engagement including site visit, engagement with library staff and Friends group, and at least one round of feedback incorporated into the final design (§1.4, §3.9).
Design and delivery of a modern, comfortable, interactive library space that is flexible and adaptable (§4.1-§4.3).
Fully accessible design that is as dementia- and autism-friendly as possible (§4.4).
Signage and graphics treated as integral design elements, not secondary (§4.5).
Replacement carpet/flooring across the main library footprint: easy to maintain, darker colours preferred to tolerate spills from warm hub, teen and children's zones (§4.6, §5.9).

Children's Library zone: storage solution(s) for craft/activity materials; standing staff desk at/near entrance; seating for story time with parents and desks for colours/homework; flexible or repositioned interactive picture book stand; retain 38 junior fiction shelves, 62 non-fiction shelves, 10 kinder boxes (existing Cantilibra shelving: 36 walled, 52 static, 16 wheeled) (§5.1).

Study Provision: expand from 12 to 18 distinct study desks, at least 10 with power access, with flexible furniture capable of forming group seating; Authority may fund separate overhead-power installation (§5.2).

Adult Shelving: approximately 210 adult fiction (including large print and spoken word), 120 non-fiction, 18 young adult, 20 local studies shelves; use shelving to separate zones; enhance existing shelving (e.g. add wheels/display panels to existing Cantilibra) in preference to full replacement; provide a distinct Young Adult zone (§5.3).

IT & Printing area: space for 6 public PCs with power/data; at least 1 PC position wheelchair-accessible/height-adjustable; multifunctional device (printer/photocopier) close to staff desk; privacy/spacing between PC users (§5.4).

Bespoke staff desk: holds 2 staff PCs with RFID pad; per PC station a minimum of 3 power points and 1 data port; additional 1 data port for Teams phone; 1 power point for till; 2 additional power for charging iPads/devices; behind-desk tambour-style storage; in-desk light stationery storage and lockable charging unit (§5.5).
Self-Service: accommodate 3 Lynsgoe Phoenix devices, each with a double-sided trolley, and 2 dump bins shared across the three (§5.6).

Events Space: flexible, separable space capable of hosting ~25-person groups (e.g. Veterans group) with seating and refreshments; whole-library flex for larger theatre-style events such as 'The Library Presents' (§5.7).
Social Seating: hotel-lobby aesthetic soft seating for 8-10 people with drinks table; accommodate the regularly accessed warm-hub trolley for hot drinks (§5.8).
First Floor Lobby: bar-stool height desk and seating with power supply; integrated poster/leaflet information display (§5.10).
Thoroughfares & Sightlines: preserve access to toilets, meeting rooms and fire exits; maintain sightlines from the main desk to avoid hidden areas (§5.11).
Sustainability built into the design methodology and furniture (environmental credentials and longevity of 5-10 years) (§3.7-§3.8, §10.1-§10.2).
Provide Risk Assessments and Method Statements specific to the first-floor shared pedestrianised shopping complex with limited delivery windows prior to site attendance (§6.2, §7.1a, §7.4).
Coordinate with Authority core maintenance contractors for building works such as power/data provision; potential optional use of Authority contractors for carpet fit-out (§7.2-§7.3).
Minimum 12-month defects period following handover (§10.4).
Warranties supplied with the bid (in response to question 2 on sustainability) (§10.3).
Mobilisation and delivery per the indicative timetable in §9 (Site visit 6 Jul 2026; fit-out install 2 Nov - 20 Dec 2026; handover 4-8 Jan 2027); final timeline agreed at contract award (§8, §9).
Handover: written documentation of materials and equipment plus in-person handover; updates during defects period (§12).
Subcontracting, if proposed, must be declared in the bid and sub-contractors must abide by all requirements (§11).
Compliance with the Modern Slavery Act and maintenance of supporting policies/procedures (§13.1).
Compliance with the Equality Act and equality, diversity and inclusion regulations with supporting policies/procedures (§14.1).
Compliance with UK GDPR where any personal data is captured during the contract; breaches reported within 72 hours (§15.1-§15.2).
Adherence to ITT Section 4 (4.1) purchase-order and invoicing processes; milestone-linked payment schedule at Contract Manager's discretion; no pre-payment/deposit (§16).

warnings.message: No CPV codes are present in the body of this tender specification document (Appendix 4). CPV signals, if required, must come from the notice/process record or a companion OCDS document.

Scored evaluation criteria are referenced (sustainability 'question 2', case studies, warranties) but no numeric weightings or scoring rubric are included in this specification; weightings are presumed to live in the companion ITT.

Document cites statutory frameworks (Modern Slavery Act, Equality Act, UK GDPR) but no British/European/ISO/BREEAM-style product standards are called out by identifier. Performance expectations (durability, accessibility, dementia-/autism-friendliness, sustainability) are stated in plain English.

Docling extraction shows section 2 (Out of Scope) text continuing after the 'Appendix 4 - Specification' header, indicating a running header/layout artefact; this is a layout quirk rather than a content split and is handled by merging the two fragments under §2.
Library footprint is quoted as 'just under 850sqm' (§3.3); this should be treated as approximate for costing purposes rather than a precise gross internal area.

Several furniture quantities (social seating for 8-10, power-point counts at bespoke desk, number of study desks on power beyond the 10 minimum) are stated as suggested or to be agreed during the final design conversation, not firm counts.
